questions.q:
The number of correct statement/s from the following is _____ .

A.Larger the activation energy, smaller is the value of the rate constant.

B. The higher is the activation energy, higher is the value of the temperature coefficient.

C. At lower temperatures, increase in temperature causes more change in the value of $k$ than at higher temperature.

D. A plot of $lnk$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ is a straight line with slope equal to $- \dfrac{Ea}{R}$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$A: k = {Ae}^{- \dfrac{Ea}{RT}}$(Arrhenius~rate equation)

As $Ea$(Activation energy) increases $k$(rate constant) decreases

B :Higher activation energy, greater is the effect of given temperature rise on rate constant 'k'. Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for the reaction to occur. When temperature increases, Kinetic Energy also increases; as temperature increases, more molecules have higher Kinetic Energy, and thus the fraction of molecules that have high enough Kinetic Energy to overcome the energy barrier also increases.

Temperature coefficient $= \dfrac{kT + 10}{kT}$

Option (C) is wrong. $\Delta k$ may be greater or lesser depending on temperature.

$D: lnk = lnA - \dfrac{Ea}{RT}$~in this equation the slope is~$- \dfrac{Ea}{R}$.

questions.q:
$2NO + 2{H}_{2} \to {N}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

The above reaction has been studied at $800 ° C$. The related data are given in the table below

Reaction~serial number Initial pressure of${H}_{2} / kPa$~ Initial Pressure
of~$NO / kPa$		 Initial rate~ \left(\dfrac{- dp}{dt}\right) / \left(kPa / s\right)$
$1$ $65 . 6$ $40 . 0$ $0 . 135$
$2$ $65 . 6$ $20 . 1$ $0 . 033$
$3$ $38 . 6$ $65 . 6$ $0 . 214$
$4$ $19 . 2$ $65 . 6$ $0 . 106$

The order of the reaction with respect to NO is____

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The rate law for the reaction& $2NO + 2{H}_{2} \to {N}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$~is

$r = k\left[{H}_{2}\right]m\left[NO\right]n$

The powers of the concentration terms m, n are the order with respect to hydrogen and nitric oxide respectively.

${r}_{1} = \left[65 . 6\right]m\left[40 . 0\right]n = 0 . 135{r}_{2} = \left[65 . 6\right]m\left[20 . 1\right]n = 0 . 033{r}_{3} = \left[38 . 6\right]m\left[65 . 6\right]n = 0 . 214{r}_{4} = \left[19 . 2\right]m\left[65 . 6\right]n = 0 . 106$

$\dfrac{r1}{r2} = \dfrac{\left[65 . 6\right]m{\left[40 . 0\right]}^{n}}{\left[65 . 6\right]m\left[20 . 1\right]n} = \dfrac{0 . 135}{0 . 033} = 4 ⇒ {2}^{n} = 4 ⇒ n = 2$

Hence, the order with~respect to~$NO$~is~$2 .$

questions.q: For a given chemical reaction& ${γ}_{1}A + {γ}_{2}B \to {γ}_{3}C + {γ}_{4}D$. Concentration of $C$~changes from $10mmol{dm}^{- 3}$ to $20mmol{dm}^{- 3}$~in~$10s .$~Rate of~appearance of $D$ is $1 . 5$~times the rate of disappearance of $B$ which is twice the rate of disappearance $A$. The rate of appearance of $D$~has been experimentally determined to be $9mmol{dm}^{- 3}s^{- 1} .$~Therefore the rate of~reaction is____mmol{dm}^{- 3}s^{- 1} .& (Nearest Integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{d\left[c\right]}{dt} = \left(\dfrac{20 - 10}{10}\right) = 1milimole / {dm}^{3}sec$

${γ}_{1}A + {γ}_{2}B \to {γ}_{3}C + {γ}_{4}D$

$\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt} = 1 . 5\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[B\right]\right) = 9milimole / {dm}^{3}sec$

\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt} \left[B\right]\right) = 2\left(- $\dfrac{d}{dt}\left[$A\right]\right)$

Rate~$= - $\dfrac{1}{\gamma1}\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt} = - \dfrac{1}{\gamma2}\dfrac{d\left[B\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{\gamma3}\dfrac{d\left[C\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{\gamma4}\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt}

(i)~\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{\gamma4}{\gamma2} \left[- $\dfrac{d \left[$B\right]}${dt}\right] = 1 . 5\left(- \dfrac{d}{dt}\left[$B\right]\right)$

\dfrac{\gamma4}{\gamma2} =$1 . 5$

(ii)~\dfrac{\gamma2}{\gamma1}\left[- \dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right] = \left(- $\dfrac{d}{dt} \left[$B\right]\right) = 2\left(- $\dfrac{d}{dt}\left[$A\right]\right)$

\dfrac{\gamma2}{\gamma1} =$2$

(iii)~\dfrac{d \left[C\right]}{dt} = $\dfrac{\gamma3}{\gamma4}\left[\dfrac{d\left[D\right]}{dt}\right]$

$1 = \dfrac{\gamma3}{\gamma4} \times9$

$\dfrac{\gamma4}{\gamma3} =9$

So, if

~${γ}_{3} = 1than{γ}_{4} = 9{γ}_{2} = 6and{γ}_{1} = 3Rateofreaction = \dfrac{1}{\gamma3}\dfrac{d [ C ]}{dt} =1mmol{dm}^{- 3}s^{- 1}$

$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
If& $K$~is known at two different temperatures the activation energy can be calculated as:

At temperature 1:~$ln{K}_{1} = - \dfrac{Ea}{RT1} + lnA$

At temperature 2:~$ln{K}_{2} = - \dfrac{Ea}{RT2} + lnA$

We can subtract one of these equations from the other:

$ln{K}_{1} - ln{K}_{2} = \left(- $\dfrac{Ea}{RT1} +$lnA\right) - \left(- $\dfrac{Ea}{RT2} +lnA\right)$

This equation can further simplified to:

$ln\dfrac{K1}{K2} = \dfrac{Ea}{R} $\$left(\dfrac{1}{T2} - \dfrac{1}{T1}\right)~

ln\dfrac{0 . 05}{0 . 03} = \dfrac{Ea}{2 . 305 \times 8 . 314} \times \left[\dfrac{1}{200} - \dfrac{1}{300}\right]$

$⇒ 0 . 22 = \dfrac{Ea}{2 . 305 \times 8 . 314} \times \left[\dfrac{1}{600}\right]$

$⇒ {E}_{a} = 2 . 3 \times8 . 3 \times600 \times0 . 22$

$⇒ {E}_{a} = 2519 . 88J ⇒ {E}_{a} = 2520J$

$

questions.solution:
The initial concentrations of $HI$ as $0 . 005, 0 . 01, \text{and}0 . 02$ mol/L, respectively, and the corresponding initial rates as given:

For the reaction, rate law is
$rate = k\left[HI\right]P$
$P$ is the order of the reaction.
From the given data
$7 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4} = k\left[0 . 05\right]P$-------(1)
$3 \times {10}^{- 3} = k\left[0 . 01\right]P$ --------(2)
$1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 2} = k\left[0 . 02\right]P$ ---------(3)
On dividing Equation (3) by equation (2)
$\dfrac{12 \times {10}^{- 3}}{3 \times {10}^{- 3}} = \dfrac{k\left[0 . 02\right]P}{k\left[0 . 01\right]P}$
$⇒ {2}^{P} = {2}^{2}$
$⇒ P = 2$

A first order reaction has the rate constant, & $k = 4 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3}s^{- 1}$. The number of correct statement/s from the following is/are Given: $log3 = 0 . 48$.

A. Reaction completes in $1000s$.
B. The reaction has a half-life of $500s$.
C. The time required for $10 %$ completion is 25 times the time required for 90%~completion.
D. The degree of dissociation is equal to \left(1 - e^{- kt}\right)$.
E. The rate and the rate constant have the same unit.

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction:
$t\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{0 . 693}{k} = \dfrac{0 . 693}{4 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3}s^{- 1}} = 150 . 65s$

For a first order reaction,
${t}_{10 %} = \dfrac{1}{K}ln \left(\dfrac{a}{a - x}\right) = \dfrac{1}{K}$ln\left(\dfrac{100}{90}\right)

${t}_{10 %} = $\dfrac{2 . 303}{K} ($log10 - log9 )$

${t}_{10 %} = $\dfrac{2 . 093}{K} \times ($0 . 04 )$


Similarly

${t}_{90 %} = $\dfrac{1}{K}$ln \left(\dfrac{100}{10}\right)$

${t}_{90 %} = \dfrac{2 . 303}{K}$

$\dfrac{t90 %}{t10 %} = \dfrac{1}{0 . 04} = 25$


We know,
$e^{kt} = \dfrac{a}{a - x}$

$\dfrac{a - x}{a} = e^{- kt}$

$x = a \left(1 - e^{- kt}\right)$

$\alpha = $\dfrac{x}{a} = \left(1 - e^{- kt}\right)$

Thus, only option (D) is correct.

$

questions.q:
The number of given statement/s which is/are correct is_____

(A) The stronger the temperature dependence of the rate constant, the higher is the activation energy.

(B) If a reaction has zero activation energy, its rate is independent of temperature.

(C) The stronger the temperature dependence of the rate constant, the smaller is the activation energy.

(D) If there is no correlation between the temperature and the rate constant then it means that the reaction has negative activation energy.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Rate constant is given by Arrhenius equation

$k = {Ae}^{- {E}_{a} / RT}$

Higher the magnitude of activation energy, stronger is the temperature dependence of the rate constant. The pre-exponential factor is a measure of the rate at which collisions occur, irrespective of their energy.& If the activation energy of reaction is zero, temperature will have no effect on the rate constant.

questions.q: For a reaction, given below is the graph of $lnkvs\dfrac{1}{T}$. The activation energy for the reaction is equal to____cal{mol}^{- 1}$.(Given : $R = 2{calK}^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1})
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Arrhenius suggested an equation which describes rate constant,$k$ as a function of temperature, T.

$k = {Ae}^{- Ea / RT}$

A=frequency factor

${E}_{a} = Activationenergy$

In the Arrhenius equation~the factor $e{~}^{- Ea / RT}$corresponds to the fraction of molecules that have kinetic energy greater than Ea

$lnk = \dfrac{-}{Ea} + lnA$

$Y = C + MX$

On plotting~$lnkagainst1 / T$~we get a straight line.The slope of the graph gives activation energy and intercept gives frequency factor

slope$= - \dfrac{Ea}{R} = \dfrac{-}{Δy}$

Slope~$= \dfrac{Ea}{R} = \dfrac{20}{5}$

${E}_{a} = 4R = 8Cal / mol$

questions.q:
The half-life of radioisotopic bromine - $82$ is $36$ hours. The fraction which remains after one day is _________\times {10}^{- 2}$.
(Given antilog $0 . 2006 = 1 . 587 )

Round off to the nearest integer
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Half life of bromine $- 82 = 36$ hours

${t}_{1 / 2} = \dfrac{0 . 693}{K}$

$K = \dfrac{0 . 693}{36} = 0 . 01925{hr}^{- 1}$

$K = \dfrac{2 . 303}{t}log\dfrac{N0}{Nt}$

\left(t = 1day = 24hr\right)$

$log\dfrac{N0}{Nt} = \dfrac{24hr \times 0 . 01925{hr}^{- 1}}{2 . 303}$

$= 0 . 2006$

$Or\dfrac{N0}{Nt} =$ anti log \left(0 . 2006\right)$

$\dfrac{N0}{Nt} = 1 . 587$

Or $\dfrac{Nt}{N0} = \dfrac{1}{1 . 587} = 0 . 630$

Hence, the fraction remain after day $= 63 \times {10}^{- 2}$
